idea: The two big products (A*S+E, S'*A+E') are about 3 million 16-bit multiply-adds each at level 128. Everything is mod 2^10, A has 10-bit entries and the secrets are small, so two coefficients fit in the 16-bit halves of one word and one multiply can update both.
change: suites/scloudplus/pqc_suite/sc_opt.inc: sc_mul_sa_e_opt and sc_mul_as_e_opt (biased secret t=s+15, (c+t*a)&0x03ff03ff, bias removed with column/row sums of A); dispatchers keep the upstream functions as *_upstream for the ref variant (scloudplus_unity.inc).
note: Measured before the shared optimized Keccak was linked into this suite, so the gain is the matrix product alone. Costs 1.2 KB more stack in encapsulation and about 10 KB in key generation (packed copy of the secret).

idea: In the AES family the rows of A are AES-128 counter blocks (29184 blocks per matrix at level 128) and the reference AES is byte-oriented C; the ESP32-C3 has an AES accelerator.
change: suites/pqmagic_common/hwaes.c (counter blocks on the accelerator in block mode: zero words written once, one write + trigger + wait + four reads per block); AES128_CTR_zero_sch dispatcher in sc_opt.inc.
note: The same image also has scloudplus-01, so this is the combined effect in the AES family; the two were not measured separately. The accelerator's own counter mode cannot be used: SCloud+ puts a little-endian counter in the first four bytes.

idea: The SM3 family failed its known-answer test on the device only: the upstream hash helper allocates up to twice the public key size and returns wrong hashes when malloc fails. The job stack (112000 bytes) took the whole large heap block.
change: Job stacks sized to what the operations use: 48 KB (level 128), 76 KB (level 192) in suites/scloudplus/pqc_suite/sc_<level>_<family>.c.
note: Not a speed change. Before: scloudplus-192-sm3 failed kat and tamper in both variants (6 fingerprints differed from the host); after: 24 checks pass, 48 of 48 fingerprints equal.

idea: A row of A in the SM3 family is 24 one-block SM3 calls of seedA||row||counter; the upstream helper allocates, copies and pads for each call. Lay the padded block out once per row and call the compression function directly.
change: sc_opt.inc: sm3_bounded_xof_seed_row dispatcher with the lean path; upstream function kept as *_upstream.
note: No separate device measurement: the only run with this change (541583 us) also had the shared optimized SM3 linked in for the first time (see scloudplus-05). Kept because it passes the known-answer tests and removes a malloc per row.

idea: The optimized Keccak and SM3 of components/prims/opt were never part of this suite's image: their strong definitions sit in the same static library as the weak defaults and the linker did not pull them in.
change: suites/pqmagic_common/component.cmake: -u pqc_keccakf1600_rv32imc_present -u pqc_sha256_hw_init -u pqc_sm3_compress_rv32 (now redundant: the prims component is linked with WHOLE_ARCHIVE).
note: Effect of the shared optimized Keccak on top of scloudplus-01. SM3 family in the same run: 780956 to 541583 us (shared SM3 plus scloudplus-04). AES family unchanged by this (156862 to 147795 us, run-to-run and code-layout difference).

idea: Same code at level 256 (n = 1184): matrix products and hardware AES.
change: suites/scloudplus_256 (builds level 256 from the same sources).
note: SHAKE family in the same run: 3257441 to 1669445 us. The SM3 family failed its known-answer test in that run for the reason of scloudplus-03 (job stack 110000 bytes left too little heap for the hash helper).

idea: Same fix as scloudplus-03 for level 256: the operations use 81 to 86 KB of stack, so a 90 KB job stack leaves the hash helper its three 16 KB buffers.
note: Did not help: with a 90 KB job stack the upstream SM3 helper still fails to allocate its three 16 to 18 KB buffers on the device, and scloudplus-256-sm3 still fails kat and tamper in both variants (it passes on the host). The 90 KB stack is left in place; SHAKE and AES at level 256 are unaffected and verified.

idea: SCloud+-256 with SM3 produced wrong keys on the device because the submission's SM3 helper could not allocate its buffers next to an 84 KB job stack, and it reports that only on stderr. Alone in an image, without the SHAKE and AES families and without the Keccak and SHA-256 backends, it should have the heap it needs.
change: new suite scloudplus_256_sm3 (SC_FAMILIES sm3, prims_off.txt: keccak, sha256); suites/scloudplus_256 keeps SHAKE and AES
note: Times in the new image: keygen 3937701 -> 2337500 us, encaps 4089949 -> 2216686 us, decaps 4089343 -> 2222951 us (ref -> opt). Done by the integrator after the line's own attempt (a smaller job stack) had not helped.
